source.snippet: I looked at our GitHub Actions monthly expenses, then at the price of a M4 Mac mini (just when they were released, and still cheap), and decided to buy one as it would pay for itself in less than a year. There are definitely still cases when buying hardware still makes sense, over renting in the cloud.

problem_statement: Engineering teams paying high monthly GitHub Actions CI/CD costs for macOS builds lack a straightforward way to evaluate when self-hosted Mac hardware becomes cheaper than cloud runners, leading to ongoing over-spend on cloud CI.
target_segment: DevOps engineers and engineering managers at software companies running macOS CI/CD pipelines on GitHub Actions or similar cloud CI providers.
notes: Buyer signal: commenter explicitly compared monthly cloud CI spend against hardware cost and bought hardware. Suggests willingness to pay for a tool that models break-even analysis for self-hosted vs cloud CI runners. Single signal but touches a recurring pain point (monthly AWS/GitHub Actions bill) in a business context.
